item.title: The Midterm Election Won’t Fix US Politics
item.description: US voters may well embrace the Democratic Party in this year’s midterm elections. But neither that outcome nor the 2028 election is likely to lead to a realignment of US politics that delivers a government capable of sustaining policies long enough to address the problems the country faces.

item.title: Europe’s Reckoning with Fossil-Fuel Insecurity
item.description: US President Donald Trump’s interventionist foreign policy will force European leaders to reconsider their dependence on American LNG supplies at the Munich Security Conference. But true energy security requires recognizing and addressing the insecurities associated with the use of hydrocarbons.

item.title: Africa Must Achieve Health Sovereignty Before the Next Pandemic
item.description: Following the outbreak of COVID-19, the Africa Centres for Disease Control received an influx of external funding to strengthen its capacity, facilitate local vaccine manufacturing, and build robust genomic networks across the continent. To prepare for the next pandemic, African governments must commit to supporting these efforts.

item.title: Could a BRICS Currency Work?
item.description: Economists have long dismissed the idea that a BRICS common currency could challenge the US dollar's role in the global economy, and for good reason. But that doesn't mean there couldn't be new common rails for settling trade between countries that want to escape the long arm of the US government.

item.title: India’s Government Must Defend Taxpayers, Not Foreign Investors
item.description: Foreign companies have reaped enormous profits from India’s fast-growing digital economy while paying little or no tax by channeling investments through offshore entities. A landmark Supreme Court ruling challenges this model, but the government’s trade agenda pulls in the opposite direction.

item.title: NATO’s Next Test
item.description: If NATO is serious about managing the Russian threat identified in its own strategy documents, it must focus its efforts where deterrence is most fragile. Lithuania's plans for a new training ground near the Suwałki corridor are thus a test case for assessing US and European resolve.

item.title: Trump the Rebel King
item.description: As a chief law-enforcement officer who has deployed gangs of criminal thugs to opposition-led cities and sued a government agency that he oversees for $10 billion, US President Donald Trump has taken the exercise of power to its most absurd extreme. He rules a state that he seeks to destroy.

item.title: When Mining Companies Leave, African Communities Pay
item.description: For decades, multinational mining companies have extracted tens of billions of dollars in profits across Africa, while sidestepping environmental and fiscal costs and leaving host communities to foot the bill. Without reliable accountability mechanisms, the clean-energy transition risks following the same trajectory.

item.title: Integration Is Africa’s Only Way Forward
item.description: Only a more united Africa can avoid “diversified dependency,” whereby primary commodities still dominate exports even as trade shifts eastward toward China and India. Heads of state and government convening in Addis Ababa for an African Union summit on February 14-15 must address the continent’s legacy of fragmentation in a new way.

item.title: Make America Trustworthy Again
item.description: The international order could still avoid a full rupture, but even temporary breaks leave lasting scars. By weaponizing tools designed to manage the global economy through international coordination, President Donald Trump is undermining US credibility and pushing allies to diversify away from American markets – perhaps permanently.
